verses.zh: 你们该效法我，像我效法基督一样。
verses.en: Be imitators of me, just as I also am of Christ.

verses.zh: 我称赞你们，因你们凡事记念我，又坚守我所传给你们的。
verses.en: I praise you[NOTE:1] because you remember me in everything and maintain the traditions just as I passed them on to you.
notes: The Western and Byzantine texts, as well as one or two Alexandrian mss (D F G Ψ 33 M latt sy), combine in reading ἀδελφοί (adelphoi, “brothers”) here, while the Alexandrian witnesses (P46 א A B C P 81 630 1175 1739 1881 2464 co) largely lack the address. The addition of ἀδελφοί is apparently a motivated reading, however, for scribes would have naturally wanted to add it to ἐπαινῶ δὲ ὑμᾶς (epainō de humas, “now I praise you”), especially as this begins a new section. On the other hand, it is difficult to explain how the shorter reading could have arisen from the longer one. Thus, on both internal and external grounds, the shorter reading is strongly preferred.

verses.zh: 我愿意你们知道，基督是各人的头；男人是女人的头；　神是基督的头。
verses.en: But I want you to know that Christ is the head of every man, and the man is the head of a woman,[NOTE:1] and God is the head of Christ.
notes: Or “the husband is the head of his wife.” The same Greek words translated “man” and “woman” can mean, as determined by context, “husband” and “wife” respectively. Such an approach is followed by NAB, TEV, NRSV, and NLT (with some variations).

verses.zh: 凡男人祷告或是讲道（或译：说预言；下同），若蒙着头，就羞辱自己的头。
verses.en: Any man who prays or prophesies with his head covered disgraces his head.

verses.zh: 凡女人祷告或是讲道，若不蒙着头，就羞辱自己的头，因为这就如同剃了头发一样。
verses.en: But any woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered disgraces her head, for it is one and the same thing as having a shaved head.

verses.zh: 女人若不蒙着头，就该剪了头发；女人若以剪发、剃发为羞愧，就该蒙着头。
verses.en: For if a woman will not cover her head, she should cut off her hair. But if it is disgraceful for a woman to have her hair cut off or her head shaved, she should cover her head.

verses.zh: 男人本不该蒙着头，因为他是　神的形像和荣耀；但女人是男人的荣耀。
verses.en: For a man should not have his head covered, since he is the image and glory of God. But the woman is the glory of the man.

verses.zh: 起初，男人不是由女人而出，女人乃是由男人而出；
verses.en: For man did not come from woman, but woman from man.

verses.zh: 并且男人不是为女人造的，女人乃是为男人造的。
verses.en: Neither was man created for the sake of woman, but woman for man.

verses.zh: 因此，女人为天使的缘故，应当在头上有服权柄的记号。
verses.en: For this reason a woman should have a symbol of authority[NOTE:1] on her head, because of the angels.[NOTE:2]
notes: Paul does not use a word specifying what type of “covering” is meant (veil, hat, etc.). The Greek word he uses here (ἐξουσία exousia; translated symbol of authority) could be (1) a figure of speech that may substitute the result (the right to participate in worship) for the appropriate appearance that makes it possible (the covered head). Or (2) it refers to the outward symbol (having the head covered) as representing the inward attitude the woman is to possess (deference to male leadership in the church).

Paul does not explain this reference to the angels, and its point is not entirely clear. It seems to reflect an awareness that angels are witnesses to church life (cf. Eph 3:10) and would be particularly sensitive to resistance against God’s created order.

verses.zh: 然而照主的安排，女也不是无男，男也不是无女。
verses.en: In any case, in the Lord woman is not independent of man, nor is man independent of woman.

verses.zh: 因为女人原是由男人而出，男人也是由女人而出；但万有都是出乎　神。
verses.en: For just as woman came from man, so man comes through woman. But all things come from God.

verses.zh: 你们自己审察，女人祷告　神，不蒙着头是合宜的吗？
verses.en: Judge for yourselves: Is it proper for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?

verses.zh: 你们的本性不也指示你们，男人若有长头发，便是他的羞辱吗？
verses.en: Does not nature[NOTE:1] itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a disgrace for him,
notes: Paul does not mean nature in the sense of “the natural world” or “Mother Nature.” It denotes “the way things are” because of God’s design.

verses.zh: 但女人有长头发，乃是她的荣耀，因为这头发是给她作盖头的。
verses.en: but if a woman has long hair, it is her glory? For her hair is given to her for a covering.[NOTE:1]
notes: No word for veil or head covering occurs in vv. 3-14 (see the note on authority in v. 10). That the hair is regarded by Paul as a covering in v. 15 is not necessarily an argument that the hair is the same as the head covering that he is describing in the earlier verses (esp. v. 10). Throughout this unit of material, Paul points out the similarities of long hair with a head covering. But his doing so seems to suggest that the two are not to be identified with each other. Precisely because they are similar they do not appear to be identical (cf. vv. 5, 6, 7, 10, 13). If head covering = long hair, then what does v. 6 mean (“For if a woman will not cover her head, she should cut off her hair”)? This suggests that the covering is not the same as the hair itself.

verses.zh: 若有人想要辩驳，我们却没有这样的规矩，　神的众教会也是没有的。
verses.en: If anyone intends to quarrel about this, we have no other practice, nor do the churches of God.

verses.zh: 我现今吩咐你们的话，不是称赞你们；因为你们聚会不是受益，乃是招损。
verses.en: Now in giving the following instruction I do not praise you, because you come together not for the better but for the worse.

verses.zh: 第一，我听说，你们聚会的时候彼此分门别类，我也稍微地信这话。
verses.en: For in the first place, when you come together as a church I hear there are divisions among you, and in part I believe it.

verses.zh: 在你们中间不免有分门结党的事，好叫那些有经验的人显明出来。
verses.en: For there must in fact be divisions among you, so that those of you who are approved may be evident.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “those approved may be evident among you.”

verses.zh: 你们聚会的时候，算不得吃主的晚餐；
verses.en: Now when you come together at the same place, you are not really eating the Lord’s Supper.

verses.zh: 因为吃的时候，各人先吃自己的饭，甚至这个饥饿，那个酒醉。
verses.en: For when it is time to eat, everyone proceeds with his own supper. One is hungry and another becomes drunk.

verses.zh: 你们要吃喝，难道没有家吗？还是藐视　神的教会，叫那没有的羞愧呢？我向你们可怎么说呢？可因此称赞你们吗？我不称赞！
verses.en: Do you not have houses so that you can eat and drink? Or are you trying to show contempt for the church of God by shaming those who have nothing? What should I say to you? Should I praise you? I will not praise you for this!

verses.zh: 我当日传给你们的，原是从主领受的，就是主耶稣被卖的那一夜，拿起饼来，
verses.en: For I received from the Lord what I also passed on to you, that the Lord Jesus on the night in which he was betrayed took bread,

verses.zh: 祝谢了，就擘开，说：「这是我的身体，为你们舍（有古卷：擘开）的，你们应当如此行，为的是记念我。」
verses.en: and after he had given thanks he broke it and said, “This is my body, which is for you. Do this in remembrance of me.”

verses.zh: 饭后，也照样拿起杯来，说：「这杯是用我的血所立的新约，你们每逢喝的时候，要如此行，为的是记念我。」
verses.en: In the same way, he also took the cup after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Do this, every time you drink it, in remembrance of me.”

verses.zh: 你们每逢吃这饼，喝这杯，是表明主的死，直等到他来。
verses.en: For every time you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until he comes.

verses.zh: 所以，无论何人，不按理吃主的饼，喝主的杯，就是干犯主的身、主的血了。
verses.en: For this reason, whoever eats the bread or drinks the cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner will be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord.

verses.zh: 人应当自己省察，然后吃这饼、喝这杯。
verses.en: A person should examine himself first,[NOTE:1] and in this way[NOTE:2] let him eat the bread and drink of the cup.
notes: The word “first” is not in the Greek text, but is implied. It has been supplied in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 因为人吃喝，若不分辨是主的身体，就是吃喝自己的罪了。
verses.en: For the one who eats and drinks without careful regard[NOTE:1] for the body eats and drinks judgment against himself.
notes: The word more literally means, “judging between, recognizing, distinguishing.”

verses.zh: 因此，在你们中间有好些软弱的与患病的，死（原文是睡）的也不少。
verses.en: That is why many of you are weak and sick, and quite a few are dead.[NOTE:1]
notes: Grk “are asleep.” The verb κοιμάω (koimaō) literally means “sleep,” but it is often used in the Bible as a euphemism for the death of a believer.

verses.zh: 我们若是先分辨自己，就不至于受审。
verses.en: But if we examined ourselves, we would not be judged.

verses.zh: 我们受审的时候，乃是被主惩治，免得我们和世人一同定罪。
verses.en: But when we are judged by the Lord, we are disciplined so that we may not be condemned with the world.

verses.zh: 所以我弟兄们，你们聚会吃的时候，要彼此等待。
verses.en: So then, my brothers and sisters,[NOTE:1] when you come together to eat, wait for one another.
notes: Grk “brothers.” See note on the phrase “brothers and sisters” in 1:10.

verses.zh: 若有人饥饿，可以在家里先吃，免得你们聚会，自己取罪。其余的事，我来的时候再安排。
verses.en: If anyone is hungry, let him eat at home, so that when you assemble it does not lead to judgment. I will give directions about other matters when I come.
